# Was the Expedia data breach a hack?

**Confirmed.** A vendor-side attack, yes: Expedia confirmed, per Skift, that attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform provider. What was taken is not established.

Incident: Expedia third-party vendor breach, Nov 2026. Also reported as the Expedia supply chain attack and the Expedia data leak. First published Nov 22, 2026; last updated Nov 22, 2026, 12:25 PM ET.

> **Not verified: initial investigation only.** Nothing on this page is absolutely confirmed. It is an early look based only on publicly available sources, and it should not be treated as verified fact. Even items labeled "Confirmed" only mean a public source reports them. Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Expedia, Skift, Cybernews, The Seattle Times or any other company, news outlet, government agency, or anyone else named.

This is the current answer, not a final verdict.

## The latest

Nov 22, 2026, 12:25 PM ET: **Expedia confirmed attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform provider; a group claims a billion records.** First build from Skift (Tier 2; partly behind a subscription) and Cybernews and The Seattle Times (all Tier 2, read Nov 22). c001 vendor attack Confirmed on Expedia's own statement to Skift and to The Seattle Times; no company page was found. c003, c005, c008, c009 Reported; c004 the billion-record claim Unverified; c006 whether customer data was taken and c007 vendor and method Not established. A larger figure of over 1TB in the sweep notes was not in either source and was dropped. The group's leak page was not visited. Privacy check done: no staff, researchers, reporters or contacts named.

## At a glance

- Status: monitoring
- Size: Regional. Unconfirmed. A group claims about a billion records; roughly 500MB has been posted, per Cybernews. Expedia has not said what was exposed.
- Who is affected: Not yet clear. A posted dataset is said to hold traveler emails, bookings and loyalty details. Expedia has not confirmed that. Watch for fake booking emails.

| Value | What | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| 1B | Records claimed | Unverified; by n0n, per Cybernews |
| 500MB+ | Posted so far | Per Cybernews |

### Known so far

- Expedia confirmed attackers got in through a compromised third-party data platform provider.

### Not known yet

- Whether the billion-record claim is true.
- Whether customer data was taken, and whose.
- Which vendor, and how the attacker got in.

## What we checked and did not find

We looked for these and did not find them as of the time of this report on Nov 22, 2026.

- An Expedia newsroom page or customer notice. The statement appears only as quotes to Skift and The Seattle Times.
- The name of the vendor, or how the attacker got in.
- Expedia saying whether customer data was taken, or confirming the posted files are real.
- Any source for a data volume over 1TB. Cybernews says the group claimed a billion records.
- Any regulator filing or customer notice.
- Any link, confirmed by Expedia or researchers, between this breach and the Qubole attack.

Part of the Skift article is behind a subscription; we read the start of Expedia's quote and Skift's summary. We did not visit the group's leak page.
